original_value: MOOC user behavior is generally studied using the data collected within platform interactions in the learning system or via outside social media platforms. It is important to understand the root causes of anomalies in MOOCs, such as the 80% attrition, less interactions within platforms and what causing the reflected behaviors beyond platforms. We study MOOC student behaviors outside the platform using ethnographic methods, mainly focusing on diary study and interviews. Two groups, 11 extreme users who have completed many MOOCs and 10 who never completed MOOC have been used to collect data. The log sheets data and interviews were analyzed using the Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) method to explore if there is a significance between these 2 groups and other qualitative comparisons to explore behavioral patterns. Our results indicated 4 behavioral patterns with insights into a significant level of learner's habits between extreme and novice users’ behaviors leading to completion or dropping. This reflects the design gaps of MOOC platforms and based on the behavioral patterns, we provide recommendations to meet the learners' needs.

result.paraphrase: MOOC user behavior is typically examined through data gathered from interactions inside the learning platform or from external social media. Understanding the causes of anomalies in MOOCs—such as 80% attrition, reduced in-platform interaction, and the behaviors reflected outside the platform—is important. In this study, we investigate MOOC student behavior outside the platform using ethnographic methods, with a primary focus on diary studies and interviews. Two groups were included: 11 extreme users who have completed many MOOCs and 10 users who have never completed a MOOC. Log sheet data and interviews were analyzed with Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) to examine whether there is a significant difference between these two groups, along with other qualitative comparisons to identify behavioral patterns. The results revealed four behavioral patterns and showed significant differences in learner habits between extreme and novice users, which relate to course completion or dropping out. These findings highlight design gaps in MOOC platforms, and we offer recommendations based on the behavioral patterns to better meet learners’ needs.
